cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The lift costs petrol and a proper conversation about why you stopped calling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Good. That gets the car moving, not us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we discuss it another day?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then today costs petrol and another postponed conversation. The second price is rising.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets petrol and explanation as two prices; A3 rules money moves only car; A5 charges B delay as another postponed conversation, increasing emotional debt under A pricing authority.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 petrol-only acceptance to preserve relational demand; A5 uses B4 delay request to increase the hurt rather than drop the offer.

relationship.evidence: B2 pays practical cost and B4 asks postponement, plausible person reluctant to discuss stopped calls.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 proposed solution into another instance of the same relational neglect, explicitly raising its price.

specificity.evidence: A1 lift, petrol and stopped calls establish both stakes; no destination required.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 moving car versus us is concise metaphor with clear two-price referents; A5 rising price is grounded by B postponement.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 accepts A1 fuel price while avoiding conversation.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 separates B2 money from the unmet emotional cost.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 asks to postpone A3 unresolved discussion.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 makes B4 postponement an added emotional charge on the same lift.
